aar_001: You can recognise it by its trunk splitting into two, then several more stems about a metre up, turning deep crimson in October. It stands east of the manor buildings in Moesgård park.
aar_002: You can recognise it by its cones standing upright on the upper branches like candles, never falling whole to the ground. It stands beside the small family cemetery in Moesgård park.
aar_003: You can recognise it by its fluted, muscled trunk, standing a little in the shade of nearby plane trees. It stands on the north side of the eastern end of Moesgård park.
aar_004: You can recognise it by its part-dead crown atop a man-made mound, weakened rather than merely old. It stands on the mound in Moesgård Museum park.
aar_005: You can recognise it by its twisted, stunted trunk, best seen bare in January or February before the leaves hide the shape. It stands in Skåde Skov, near Ørnereden.
aar_006: You can recognise it by standing opposite the entrance to Viby Church's churchyard, on Kirkevej, a short walk from the light rail stop.
aar_007: You can recognise it by its crown spreading wide sideways, grown with nothing ever crowding it from the light. It stands at the roadside on Elmehøjvej.
